pests.name: Bees, wasps and hornets
pests.title: Bee and Wasp Nest Removal in Nairobi and Kenya | Stermont Arcade
pests.desc: Paper wasps, mud daubers, honey bees, carpenter bees and large hornet-like wasps in Kenyan homes and compounds. Safety, nests and removal.
pests.h1: Bee, wasp and hornet nest control in Nairobi and across Kenya
pests.lead: Stay away from the nest, keep children and pets indoors, and call us. Do not try to burn, smoke or spray a nest yourself.
intro: Stinging insects build nests under roofs, in eaves, in wall cavities, in trees, on gates and inside meter boxes, and they defend them. A nest the size of a fist can hold dozens of wasps, and a bee colony in a wall can hold tens of thousands. Most stings happen when someone disturbs a nest without knowing it is there, for example while pruning, painting or cleaning gutters.

Not every stinging insect is a pest, and some, such as honey bees, are useful. African honey bees are known for defending their nest fiercely and can attack in numbers, so a wall colony needs care. Where it is possible, the better outcome is to move the bees alive with a beekeeper, and we say so when that is the case.

varieties.d: Slim, long-legged wasps that build open, umbrella-shaped paper nests under eaves, beams, window frames and shelters. They sting when the nest is disturbed.
Solitary wasps that build small mud tubes or pots on walls and ceilings. They are not aggressive and are mostly an untidiness problem.
Colonies in hollow walls, roof spaces, water meter boxes and trees. African honey bees can react strongly if disturbed, and a swarm should be left alone and reported.
Large, shiny black or blue-black bees that drill round holes in dry timber to nest. They are seldom aggressive but can damage fascia boards, pergolas and beams.
Big, strongly marked wasps that people often call hornets. They build large paper or ground nests and should be left to a trained person to handle.

signs: A steady flow of wasps or bees going in and out of one spot in a wall, roof or tree
A visible paper nest, mud tubes or round holes in timber
A buzzing or humming sound inside a wall
Wax or honey stains seeping through plaster or ceiling boards
Dead bees or wasps on the floor near a window or light
Stings to people or pets near the same place on more than one occasion
pests.riskTitle: Health risks and why it matters
risk: A sting is painful and for most people the pain and swelling fade within a day. Multiple stings can cause serious illness, and some people are allergic. Swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing, dizziness or collapse after a sting are emergencies, so get to a hospital right away. Children, older people, and people with allergies are the most at risk.
causes: Sheltered, undisturbed spots under roofs, eaves and in quiet corners
Small gaps in walls, roofs and fascia boards that give access to cavities
Flowering plants, fruit trees and water sources nearby
Untreated dry timber, which is attractive to carpenter bees
Old nests that attract new queens in the next season
prevent: Inspect eaves, sheds and gutters regularly, and remove small new nests early in the season by calling us, not by yourself
Seal gaps and holes in walls and roofs and paint or treat exposed timber
Keep bins covered and clean up fruit that has fallen
Do not leave sugary drinks open outdoors
If you find a nest, keep children and pets away and put up a warning
Wear protective clothing for any garden work around trees and eaves
pests.scope: We remove or treat wasp nests and carpenter bee damage. For honey bee colonies in walls and roofs we recommend, where possible, a beekeeper who can move the colony alive. We do not advise burning, smoking or spraying a nest yourself.
approach: We inspect the nest from a safe distance, identify the insect, and plan the work. Wasp nests are usually treated at dusk or dawn, when most of the colony is inside and calmer, and then the nest is removed after activity has stopped. For wall and roof colonies, we explain whether removal of the nest and combs is needed so that other insects and rodents are not drawn to the old honey.
Please keep everyone indoors on the day, close windows nearest the nest, and move pets inside. We tell you when the area is safe.

faqs.q: Is it safe to remove a wasp nest myself?
faqs.a: It is risky. Wasps defend the nest, and a disturbed nest can cause many stings. Keep away and call us.

faqs.q: What should I do after a sting?
faqs.a: Wash the area, remove the sting if it is in the skin and apply a cold compress. If there is swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing, dizziness or many stings, go to a hospital immediately.

faqs.q: Will you kill the honey bees in my wall?
faqs.a: Where possible we recommend relocation by a beekeeper. If that is not possible, we discuss the options and the need to remove the comb so that it does not attract other pests.

faqs.q: Do carpenter bees harm my timber?
faqs.a: They drill round holes and tunnels in dry timber, which can weaken beams over the years. Treating and painting the wood helps stop them.

pests.name: Spiders
pests.title: Spider Control in Nairobi and Kenya | Stermont Arcade
pests.desc: House spiders, huntsman spiders, button spiders and baboon spiders in Kenya: which are harmless, which need care and how to reduce them.
pests.h1: Spider control in Nairobi and across Kenya
pests.lead: Most spiders are harmless and eat other pests. A few need caution. We help you reduce the ones you do not want indoors.
intro: Almost all spiders eat insects, and a house with a few spiders usually has fewer flies and mosquitoes. People call for help when there are lots of webs, when large spiders appear suddenly, or when a bite or a child's fear makes the problem urgent.

A small number of spiders in Africa can cause medically significant bites. In Kenya these include widow-type spiders, called button spiders, and large burrowing ground spiders sometimes called baboon spiders in dry rural areas. The sensible rule is: do not handle spiders with bare hands, and get medical advice for a painful bite that spreads or causes illness.

varieties.d: Small, harmless web-builders in corners, under furniture and around windows. They are mostly a cleaning matter.
Large, flat, long-legged spiders that run quickly on walls and ceilings and do not build webs to catch prey. They look alarming, but are rarely harmful.
Dark, round-bodied spiders in the widow group, found in sheltered places such as outbuildings, wood piles and under stones. Their bite can cause pain and illness and needs a medical check.

varieties.n: Baboon spiders and large ground spiders
varieties.d: Large, hairy burrowing spiders found mainly in dry rural areas. They bite when handled or trapped, and a bite should be checked by a health worker.

signs: Webs in corners, behind furniture, under eaves and in window frames
Egg sacs, which look like small silk balls, in corners and sheltered places
A large spider running across a wall or floor at night
A bite with pain, swelling or a mark, especially after moving stored boxes, firewood or garden items
Burrows with silk lining in the soil in dry rural plots
Many small flies and insects, which feed spiders and keep them near the house
pests.riskTitle: Health risks and why it matters
risk: Most spider bites are minor and heal by themselves. A bite that is very painful, spreads, causes muscle cramps, sweating, fever or vomiting, or happens in a small child, should be checked by a health worker without delay. Keep the spider if it is safe to do so, or a photo, to help the health worker.
causes: Plenty of insects as prey, especially around lights
Clutter, stored boxes, firewood and garden items that provide hiding places
Gaps around doors, windows and vents
Long grass, bushes and creepers touching the walls
Undisturbed outbuildings, garages and stores
prevent: Remove webs and egg sacs regularly with a broom or vacuum and empty the bag outdoors
Reduce clutter and store items in sealed plastic boxes off the floor
Seal gaps around doors, windows and pipes and fit screens
Shake out shoes, gloves and clothes that have been left in a store, garage or outside
Cut back vegetation from the walls and keep firewood away from the house
Switch off outdoor lights when not needed, because lights attract insects and then spiders
approach: We inspect the house and outbuildings, remove webs and egg sacs where we can and treat the cracks, eaves and sheltered corners where spiders hide and where their insect prey live. Reducing the insects reduces the spiders.
For button spiders and other medically significant spiders in stores and yards, we advise on safe clearing, and we ask you to tell us about children, pets and the layout of the plot.

faqs.q: Are house spiders dangerous?
faqs.a: Most are harmless to people and eat other insects. A few species, such as button spiders, need caution, and a painful or spreading bite should be seen by a health worker.

faqs.q: Why do I find spiders in the bathroom?
faqs.a: They come looking for small insects, which are drawn to moisture. Repairing leaks and sealing gaps reduces both.

faqs.q: Do you remove spiders by hand?
faqs.a: We remove webs and egg sacs and treat the hiding places. For large or unusual spiders, we advise you to keep away and call us.

faqs.q: What should I do after a spider bite?
faqs.a: Wash the area and keep it clean. If there is severe pain, spreading redness, cramps, sweating, fever or vomiting, or if the person is a child, go to a hospital or clinic.

pests.name: Scorpions
pests.title: Scorpion Control in Kenya | Stermont Arcade
pests.desc: Scorpions in dry parts of Kenya: where they hide, what a sting can do, how to find them with a UV torch and how to keep them out of homes and schools.
pests.lead: Scorpions hide by day and hunt at night. Shake out shoes and clothes, seal the gaps, and call us for an inspection of the building and compound.
intro: Scorpions are nocturnal predators. They hide under stones, logs, bark, roof tiles, in cracks and in piles of rubble by day, and come out at night to catch insects. In dry and semi-arid parts of Kenya they can enter houses, schools, tents and stores, and they sometimes hide in shoes, bedding and clothes left on the floor.

A scorpion sting is painful, and for most healthy adults the pain and local swelling pass. Some species have venom that is dangerous, especially to small children, so any sting in a child, or a sting followed by sweating, drooling, vomiting, muscle twitching or trouble breathing, needs urgent medical care.

varieties.d: Dark scorpions with thick tails and slender pincers, found in dry areas of eastern and northern Africa. Some species have venom that is a medical concern.
Large scorpions with strong pincers that live in burrows or under rocks. Stings are painful but usually less dangerous than those from thick-tailed species.
Smaller scorpions that hide in walls, roofs and under objects. Small size does not mean a safe sting, so treat any scorpion with caution.

signs: A scorpion seen in a bathroom, on a wall, under a mat, or in a shoe
Scorpions hiding under stones, boards, bricks, roof tiles, logs and rubble in the compound
A sting at night or in the morning on a hand or foot when putting on shoes or reaching under an object
Many insects around the house, which are their prey
Cracks and gaps in walls, thatch or roofs that let them in
Glowing blue-green shapes under a UV torch at night, which is how they are found in the dark
pests.riskTitle: Health risks and why it matters
risk: Scorpion stings cause immediate pain, swelling and numbness. In children and in some species, they can cause serious symptoms. Take any child, and any adult with unusual symptoms, to a hospital quickly. Do not cut the wound or apply a tourniquet. Keep the person calm and still, and bring the scorpion if it can be done safely.
causes: Dry rural and peri-urban plots with stones, bricks, rubble and firewood
Gaps in walls, doors and under roofs, and thatched or loose roofs
Plenty of insects around the house for them to eat
Clothes, shoes and bedding left on the floor
Building sites and stores with piles of timber, tiles and stone
prevent: Shake out shoes, boots, clothes, towels and bedding before using them
Sleep with bedding off the floor and tuck in nets
Seal gaps around doors, windows and pipes and fit door sweeps
Clear rubble, timber, bricks and rubbish from the plot and keep firewood away from the house
Reduce insects by repairing lights, bins and leaks
Wear closed shoes and use a torch outdoors at night
approach: We inspect at night with a UV torch, where possible, to find where scorpions hide and travel. We treat entry points, cracks and the places they shelter, and we advise on clearing rubble and sealing the building. Reducing their insect prey is part of the plan.
Scorpions are hardy, so a follow-up visit is usual. For schools and children's homes in scorpion areas, we recommend regular inspections.

faqs.q: How serious is a scorpion sting?
faqs.a: Most stings in healthy adults cause pain and swelling only. Stings in children, and stings with sweating, vomiting, drooling, twitching or trouble breathing, are emergencies. Go to a hospital.

faqs.q: Can I find scorpions at night myself?
faqs.a: A UV torch makes them glow, but do not handle them. Keep your distance and call us.

faqs.q: How do I keep scorpions out of my shoes?
faqs.a: Keep shoes off the floor or in a closed box, and shake them out before wearing.

faqs.q: Do you treat schools and camps?
faqs.a: Yes. We take requests from all 47 counties. Send your location and the type of building on WhatsApp for a quote.

pests.name: Centipedes and millipedes
pests.title: Centipede and Millipede Control in Kenya | Stermont Arcade
pests.desc: Why centipedes and millipedes come indoors after rain, how to tell them apart, which bite or irritate, and how to keep them out of homes and gardens.
pests.h1: Centipede and millipede control in Nairobi and across Kenya
pests.lead: They come in when it is wet. Dry out the damp spots, seal the gaps and treat the edges of the house.
intro: Centipedes and millipedes are not insects. They are many-legged creatures that live in damp soil, leaf litter, mulch, under stones and logs. After heavy rain, flooding or a dry spell, they move toward buildings looking for shelter and moisture. That is why they appear in bathrooms, ground-floor rooms, garages and bedrooms in the rainy season.

They look alike to many people but behave differently. Centipedes are fast, flat predators with one pair of legs per segment, and the large ones can give a painful bite. Millipedes are slow, rounded and have two pairs of legs per segment. They do not bite, but they curl up and release a fluid that can irritate skin and eyes.

varieties.d: Flat, fast, brownish or reddish centipedes that can reach 10 to 20 cm. They hunt insects at night and can bite hard if handled or trapped in clothing and bedding.
Smaller, slender, fast centipedes with long legs found in damp rooms and bathrooms. They eat other small pests and are seldom harmful.
Slow, cylindrical, dark or reddish-brown, curling into a coil when disturbed. They feed on decaying plant matter and are sometimes seen in large numbers after rain.

signs: Fast, flat centipedes in bathrooms, sinks, bedrooms and storage areas at night
Slow-moving coiled millipedes on floors, patios and door thresholds after rain
Many millipedes trapped in bathtubs, drains and the base of walls
A painful bite or sting-like pain from something in clothes, shoes or bedding
A skin stain or irritation after handling a millipede, or irritated eyes after rubbing them with unwashed hands
Damp patches, leaf litter and mulch against the walls
risk: A centipede bite is painful, may swell and usually settles within a few days. Wash the bite and seek medical advice if swelling spreads or the person feels unwell. Millipedes do not bite, but their fluid can irritate skin and eyes, so wash your hands after touching one. Neither carries common diseases, but a large number indoors points to a damp problem or a gap around the house.
causes: Heavy rain, flooding or sudden changes in the weather that move them toward buildings
Damp soil, mulch, compost, leaf litter and wood piles against the walls
Poor drainage and leaking taps and pipes
Gaps under doors, around pipes and in air vents
Plenty of insects as prey for centipedes
prevent: Keep mulch, leaf litter and compost at least a short distance from the walls
Fix leaks and improve drainage around the house
Seal gaps under doors and around pipes and fit door sweeps
Sweep or vacuum millipedes and centipedes and throw them away outdoors
Reduce insects, which feed centipedes
Do not handle them with bare hands
approach: We inspect the building edge, drains, gutters and damp areas, and treat the perimeter and the entry points, and the shelters where they gather. We advise on fixing moisture because without that the numbers return after the next rain.
We take requests for gardens, homes, schools and estates, and give a follow-up check after heavy rain where needed.

faqs.q: Why are there so many millipedes after rain?
faqs.a: Rain drives them out of the soil and toward dry shelter. Sweep them up and treat the entry points to the house.

faqs.q: Is a centipede bite dangerous?
faqs.a: Usually it is painful and local, and settles in a few days. Seek help if swelling spreads, if the person is a small child or if they feel unwell.

faqs.q: Do millipedes bite?
faqs.a: No, but they can release an irritating fluid. Wash your hands after touching them and keep them away from your eyes.

faqs.q: Will drying out the house remove them?
faqs.a: Reducing moisture helps a great deal. Treatment around the edges of the house is used as well.

pests.name: Silverfish
pests.title: Silverfish Control in Nairobi and Kenya | Stermont Arcade
pests.desc: Silverfish in books, paper, wardrobes and bathrooms. Why they like damp rooms, the damage they cause and how to control them in homes, offices and archives.
pests.h1: Silverfish control in Nairobi and across Kenya
pests.lead: Silverfish eat starch in paper, book glue and fabric. Cut the humidity, store paper in sealed boxes and treat the hiding places.
intro: Silverfish are small, wingless, silver-grey insects, about 12 to 19 mm long, with a tapered body and three tails. They run fast, avoid light, and hide in cracks and behind skirting boards, in cupboards, bathrooms, kitchens and storage rooms. They are mostly active at night, so many people only notice them when a light comes on or when they find damage.

Silverfish eat starchy and sugary materials, which means paper, cardboard, book bindings, wallpaper paste, photographs, cotton and linen fabrics, and some dry foods. They do not bite or spread disease, but they damage documents, books, clothing and stored items, which is why they matter in offices, schools, churches, libraries and homes with family papers.

varieties.d: The typical silverfish, found in damp, dark places and favoured by warm, humid rooms.
Related insects that like warmer places such as near ovens, hot water pipes and boiler rooms.
Similar-looking insects that may be found outdoors and sometimes enter buildings. We identify them during the inspection.

signs: Small silver-grey insects darting away when you move a box, book or cloth
Irregular holes, scrapes and surface damage on paper, book spines, labels and wallpaper
Yellowish stains and tiny dark droppings like black pepper in storage boxes and drawers
Shed skins in cupboards, bookshelves and bath areas
Damage to cotton and linen clothes, especially with starch or stains
A damp or musty room, leaking pipe or condensation near where they are seen
risk: Silverfish do not harm people, but they can ruin documents, old photos, certificates, books and clothing. Offices with filing rooms, schools with exercise books, and churches or families with old records should treat them early because the damage cannot be repaired.
causes: High humidity from leaks, poor ventilation, bathrooms, kitchens and condensation
Cardboard boxes and paper stored on the floor or against damp walls
Starchy materials such as book glue, wallpaper paste and laundry starch
Cracks and gaps behind skirting boards and in shelves
Items brought in on cardboard boxes, books and second-hand furniture
prevent: Reduce humidity with fixes for leaks and better ventilation, and use a dehumidifier in damp rooms if you can
Store papers, photographs and books in sealed plastic boxes, off the floor and away from outside walls
Replace cardboard storage boxes with plastic ones
Keep wardrobes dry, and wash and dry clothes fully before storing them
Seal gaps behind skirting and shelves
Check storage areas every few months
approach: We inspect the rooms, boxes and shelves where silverfish are found, find the damp source and treat the cracks and hiding places. We do not spray onto books, papers or clothing. We tell you what to move and how to store it afterwards.
Because the humidity is part of the cause, treatment only works well with a plan to dry out the space. For offices and archives, we agree a regular inspection.

faqs.q: Do silverfish bite people?
faqs.a: No. They do not bite or spread disease. They damage paper, books and fabrics.

faqs.q: Why do I see silverfish in the bathroom?
faqs.a: Bathrooms are damp and warm, and they have cracks and starchy items. Improve ventilation and fix leaks.

faqs.q: Can you protect my archive?
faqs.a: We treat the room and shelving and advise on sealed storage. We do not apply products directly onto records.

faqs.q: Are silverfish a sign of dirt?
faqs.a: No. They are a sign of damp and stored paper. Clean homes get them too.

pests.name: Clothes moths
pests.title: Clothes Moth Control in Nairobi and Kenya | Stermont Arcade
pests.desc: Webbing and casemaking clothes moths in wardrobes, carpets and woollens. Signs, why larvae damage wool and silk, and how to protect clothes and carpets.
pests.h1: Clothes moth control in Nairobi and across Kenya
pests.lead: It is the larvae, not the adult moths, that eat holes in wool, silk, fur and feathers. Clean, store sealed and treat the cupboard.
intro: Clothes moths are small, buff-coloured moths, around 6 to 8 mm long, that avoid light and run or flutter low in dark cupboards. The adults do not feed. The damage comes from their larvae, which eat natural fibres that contain keratin: wool, cashmere, silk, fur, felt, feathers and hair, and sometimes cotton or synthetic blends soiled with food, sweat or body oils.

Because the larvae live in dark corners, a wardrobe can be affected for months before anyone sees a hole. Woollen suits, school jumpers, blankets, carpets, rugs, upholstered furniture, taxidermy and piano felts are all at risk, especially if they are stored dirty or left undisturbed.

varieties.d: The larvae spin silk webbing and tunnels on the fabric as they feed, leaving patches of damage and silky mats.
The larvae live inside a small silk case that they carry with them as they feed, often seen on walls and fabric.
Different moths that eat dry food, grains and flour. They need food-store treatment, not clothes treatment.

signs: Irregular holes and thinned patches in wool, silk and fur items
Silky webbing, tunnels or small cases on the fabric, in seams and in corners
Tiny pale larvae with dark heads, small black droppings and shed skins
Small buff moths in wardrobes, which avoid light and flutter low
Bare patches in carpets, especially under furniture and along edges
Damage in the folds of stored blankets and in clothes that have been left unused for a long time
risk: Clothes moths do not harm people, but the damage to good clothing, school uniforms, blankets and carpets cannot be undone and can be costly. They are more of a problem in cool highland homes where woollens are used, and in stores of second-hand clothes.
causes: Unwashed or lightly soiled wool and silk items stored for a long time
Dark, still, undisturbed corners in wardrobes, under beds and in boxes
Dust, hair and lint that collect along the edges of carpets and under furniture
Second-hand clothes, blankets and rugs brought into the home
Cupboards that are rarely opened or aired
prevent: Wash or dry-clean woollens and silks before storing them, because food and sweat stains attract larvae
Store clothes in sealed plastic boxes or tight bags, not open cardboard
Air, brush and shake clothes and blankets in the sun now and then
Vacuum carpets, under furniture and wardrobe floors, paying attention to edges
Check stored items every month or two
Inspect second-hand clothes and rugs before they go into your wardrobe
approach: We inspect wardrobes, carpets, rugs and the corners where larvae live, and treat the cupboard, carpet edges and cracks. We do not spray onto clothes. We give you a list of items to wash, brush or seal and when to put them back.
For large stores, we arrange an inspection and a plan for the whole space.

faqs.q: Do the moths I see eat my clothes?
faqs.a: No. The adults do not feed. The larvae cause the damage, so finding and treating the larvae and their hiding places matters most.

faqs.q: Does washing remove clothes moths?
faqs.a: Washing and drying at a high heat usually removes eggs and larvae from items that can take it. Dry cleaning is an option for delicate items.

faqs.q: Can they damage carpets?
faqs.a: Yes, especially wool carpets and the areas under furniture and along walls.

faqs.q: Are mothballs necessary?
faqs.a: Our advice is to rely on cleaning, sealed storage and treatment of the cupboard. If you use mothballs, follow the label strictly and keep them away from children and pets.

pests.name: Carpet beetles
pests.title: Carpet Beetle Control in Nairobi and Kenya | Stermont Arcade
pests.desc: Carpet beetle larvae damage wool, fur, feathers and leather. Learn the signs, where they breed and how to get rid of them in homes and stores.
pests.h1: Carpet beetle control in Nairobi and across Kenya
pests.lead: The adults feed on flowers outdoors. The hairy larvae indoors eat wool, fur, feathers, leather and dead insects. Find the source and clean.
intro: Carpet beetles are small, rounded beetles, about 2 to 4 mm long. Adults may be mottled, black or patterned and are often found on windowsills, because they are drawn to light and fly outdoors to feed on pollen. The larvae are the pest: they are small, hairy and brownish, and they crawl in dark places eating animal-based materials.

They feed on wool carpets, rugs, blankets, felt, silk, fur, feathers, leather, taxidermy, pet hair and the dried remains of insects. They can also infest stored dry foods such as flour, cereals and pet food. A common hidden source is a dead insect or bird nest in a roof or wall void.

varieties.d: A small, round beetle with a mottled pattern. The larvae are hairy and brown with a carrot shape and feed on wool and fur.
A shiny black or dark brown beetle. The larvae are elongate with a tail of hairs and feed on wool, fur and stored foods.
A small beetle whose larvae feed on upholstery, carpets and similar materials in homes.

signs: Small beetles on windowsills in spring and summer
Shed larval skins, which look like tiny, hairy brown tubes, in corners, drawers and under furniture
Irregular bare patches or holes in wool carpets and rugs
Damage to fur, feathers, felt, leather and stored woollens
Skin irritation or small itchy marks from larval hairs, which are sometimes mistaken for bed bug bites
Larvae or skins in stored flour, cereals or pet food
risk: Carpet beetles damage valuable items and carpets and can spread through the home along skirting boards and under furniture. They do not spread disease, but some people get itchy skin from larval hairs. Fixing the source, such as a dead insect nest in the roof, is key to stopping repeat outbreaks.
causes: Dead insects, bird nests and rodent nests in the roof, wall voids and under floors
Accumulated hair, lint, dust and pet fur under furniture and along skirting boards
Stored woollens, fur, feathers and leather that are rarely cleaned
Open windows that let adults in, or flowers brought indoors
Contaminated flour, cereals or pet food stored in open packets
prevent: Vacuum carpets, rugs, upholstery, skirting boards and under furniture regularly
Wash or dry-clean woollens and store them in tight containers
Store flour, cereals and pet food in sealed containers
Clear old bird, wasp and rodent nests from roof spaces and wall voids
Screen windows and keep cut flowers out of bedrooms
Check stored items regularly
approach: We inspect carpets, cupboards, edges and voids, look for the source, such as an old nest, and treat the edges, cracks and storage spaces. We explain what to clean, wash or discard.
Cleaning matters as much as treatment: a vacuum and a wash remove larvae and food sources that products cannot reach.

faqs.q: Are carpet beetles the same as bed bugs?
faqs.a: No. They are different insects. Carpet beetle larvae eat fabric and food, while bed bugs feed on blood. The larval hairs can cause itchy marks, which is why people confuse them.

faqs.q: Where do they come from?
faqs.a: Often from outdoors as adults in flight, or from a hidden dead insect or old nest in a roof or wall void.

faqs.q: Can they damage my carpet?
faqs.a: Yes. Wool carpets and rugs are common targets, particularly under furniture and along edges.

faqs.q: Do I need to throw my items away?
faqs.a: Not always. Many items can be washed, dry-cleaned or sealed. We advise item by item.
